Both halves are done. Here's the full picture:

## Verification: A+B was followed and completed

The four commits (51f76c4 feature, bed4178 dev tooling, 8398e2b sync/archive, b413120 CI portability) implement the plan faithfully — all 32/32 tasks complete (the original 26 plus an amendment group added mid-change), the change archived, both delta specs synced to main specs with Covered-by evidence pointers, `openspec validate --all` passing, and 667 unit tests green just now. Every planned artifact exists where the design said it would: pure classifier ([classify.ts](src/classify.ts)), WeakMap parse cache, stats surface, filter adapter, pure escalation math ([escalate.ts](src/escalate.ts)), and e2e suites 60/61 driven by real input.

Deviations from plan are all documented, and notably every surprise resolved toward *more* safety — the shape default-permit was designed to tolerate:

- **D3 provenance hypothesis was partly wrong**: external `Vault.process` reconciliation arrives *with* a `userEvent: "set"` annotation (design assumed none); classifier tightened, spec text amended before sync.
- **Desktop undo bypasses the filter entirely** — stronger than "classified programmatic"; platform-dependent under mobile emulation, so the e2e asserts the portable half everywhere.
- **Nested-editor degeneracy confirmed**; the StateField fallback was never needed. Perf came in ~10× under budget; the incremental-parse fallback was never needed either.
- **Three D4 amendments from the manual passes** (gap-line trigger, expand-only invariant, uniform multi-range escalation) were adopted in-change with spec updates — process working as intended.
- **Two honest gaps carried forward**: find-and-replace and HTML5 drag-drop couldn't be automated (harness limits), flagged in the synced spec; and `boundary-crossing-edit` got zero perf samples — both now matter more for Phase C and are addressed in it.

## Phase C proposal: `outline-edit-enforcement`

Created and validated at [openspec/changes/outline-edit-enforcement/](openspec/changes/outline-edit-enforcement/), all four artifacts complete. The shape:

- **[proposal.md](openspec/changes/outline-edit-enforcement/proposal.md)** — close the invariant for *mutations*: the counted-but-passed `boundary-crossing-edit` class gains pass/rewrite/veto verdicts. One new capability (`node-edit-enforcement`), two modified (`transaction-classification` — its "never modifies text" contract is superseded by a narrowed per-class version; `structural-operations` — extended with `deleteSubtrees`/`mergeNodes`/`insertSubtrees` pure ops). Selection UX (Track 2 of [13-selection-follow-ups.md](docs/research/13-selection-follow-ups.md)) is explicitly out of scope, as requested.
- **[design.md](openspec/changes/outline-edit-enforcement/design.md)** — the key decisions, each grounded in a Phase A/B learning: verdicts as a pure layer on the existing classification seam; rewrites as *compositions of new tree ops* inheriting the property-test guarantees; escalate-then-delete so stale mid-node selections (the programmatic pass-through case) can't produce half-node deletions; Backspace/Delete merges recognized by *edit shape*, deliberately not keymaps; the paste rule biased to pass on ambiguity (a wrong pass is editable, a wrong rewrite is surprising); veto cues emitted outside the filter; and narrow default-deny only inside the recognized user-edit class — Q6's sync pass-through stays inviolable.
- **Specs** — the trickiest delta is [transaction-classification](openspec/changes/outline-edit-enforcement/specs/transaction-classification/spec.md): rather than quietly weakening "Document text is never modified by this layer," it's formally REMOVED with a migration note and replaced by "Text modification is confined to enforced verdicts," so the archive sync stays honest.
- **[tasks.md](openspec/changes/outline-edit-enforcement/tasks.md)** — 5 groups, 22 tasks, ordered ops → verdict layer → wiring → evidence → closure. Task 1.2 pins the per-kind merge table in the spec *before* implementing it (the design's biggest open question), 4.5 produces the first-ever perf samples for the enforced path, 4.6 retries the two automation gaps with mandatory scripted manual fallback, and 5.4 keeps the A+B amendment loop.

One thing to look at before implementation: the per-kind merge algebra (which cross-kind joins are expressible vs. vetoed) is deliberately left as a spec-time decision inside task 1.2 — it's the one place where your judgment on feel (how often a plain Backspace should bounce off a veto) will shape the rules more than the math does. Ready for `/opsx:apply` when you are.
